tagline: A year-round luxury island below the hurricane belt — calm leeward water, heavy cruise + resort demand, and no foiling incumbent.
summary: Curaçao is the largest of the Dutch ABC islands, sitting ~12°N off the Venezuelan coast and below the main Atlantic hurricane belt — giving its sheltered leeward (south/west) coast rare year-round calm-water economics. The island drew roughly 1.57M total visitors in 2024, including 834,890 cruise passengers across 328 calls, anchored by the UNESCO-listed Willemstad waterfront and a premium leeward resort strip (Sandals Royal Curaçao, Baoase, the Piscadera cluster, Jan Thiel). Today every airport, cruise-pier and resort transfer runs on diesel road shuttles or conventional boats; there is no fast electric water tier and no foiling operator, making Curaçao a clean entry node for a captive resort-and-cruise water network.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire intra-Curaçao network — airport, cruise-pier and resort legs are all short, calm, leeward runs squarely in range, with the bonus of year-round, below-the-hurricane-belt operation.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) is the vessel for the longer island-to-island reaches (Curaçao↔Aruba) as the network scales beyond the captive Curaçao core.

signature_routes: Willemstad cruise pier ↔ Piscadera / Spanish Water
competitive_landscape: Diesel road shuttles and conventional dive/excursion boats serve Curaçao today; there is no fast electric water tier and no foiling incumbent. The leeward resort-transfer market is fragmented across road operators — a clean consolidation opportunity for a single silent waterway.
seasonality: The leeward (south/west) coast is calm roughly 90% of the time and sits below the main hurricane belt, supporting rare year-round operation. Klein Curaçao is the seasonal exception, carrying 5–7 ft swell and offered only in the calm-water months.
regulatory_note: Curaçao is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, regulated by the Maritime Authority Curaçao and the Curaçao Ports Authority. The Curaçao Tourism Board actively promotes high-value, low-impact tourism, which favors zero-emission, low-wake vessels.
